name: Maasai

population.definition: Kenya only: people counted as Maasai by ethnic community in the 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census, as reported by the press from KNBS results (KNBS table itself not read). No Tanzanian figure found; Tanzania's census does not appear in readable sources.

source.title: Kenya's 10 Most Populous Communities
source.author: Samuel Mbataru
source.quote: the Maasai closed the top ten list with a population of 1,189,522 people

facts.claim: Kenya's census counted 154,906 Maasai in 1969 (1.43% of the population) and 1,189,522 in 2019 (about 2.5%), roughly seven-fold.

source.title: Kikuyu, Luo and Kamba numbers down while Somalis, Maasai and Kalenjin up
source.author: PhD student, Population Studies and Research Institute (name not shown)
source.quote: about seven times its initial population

facts.claim: Glottolog lists Maasai as a language of Kenya and Tanzania, classified within Eastern Nilotic (Nuclear Maa) and not endangered.
A Mara study (2012) says leasing land to tourism investors through conservancies can keep rangeland areas together, but subdivision of Kenya's rangelands has tended to benefit elites.

source.title: Conservation and ecotourism on privatised land in the Mara, Kenya: The case of conservancy land leases
source.publisher: LDPI Working Paper 9, University of the Western Cape repository
source.author: Claire Bedelian
source.quote: land leases do however keep the lands they cover together

timeline.claim: Maasai elders signed the 1904 agreement with the British, which was pledged to last 'so long as the Maasai as a race shall exist'; several sections were moved into Laikipia and a Southern Reserve.

source.title: 2023 Marks 110 Years Since the Maasai Case 1913: Does it Still Matter?
source.author: Lotte Hughes
source.quote: so long as the Maasai as a race shall exist

timeline.claim: A second agreement (1911) moved the northern Maasai from Laikipia to the Southern Reserve; the author says it was signed by Seggi, not Olonana, and estimates the Maasai lost at least half of their land.

source.title: 2023 Marks 110 Years Since the Maasai Case 1913: Does it Still Matter?
source.author: Lotte Hughes

timeline.claim: Maasai plaintiffs challenged the agreements in court; the High Court dismissed the case in May 1913 and the appeal failed in December 1913, the judges treating the agreements as treaties (Acts of State).

source.title: 2023 Marks 110 Years Since the Maasai Case 1913: Does it Still Matter?
source.author: Lotte Hughes

timeline.claim: Amnesty International says Maasai were moved from Serengeti National Park to Loliondo in 1959 and were later repeatedly evicted. (Paraphrase from a reading of the page; exact wording not captured, verify before use.)

source.title: Tanzania: Authorities brutally violated Maasai amid forced evictions from ancestral lands

timeline.claim: Nine UN experts said a plan to turn 1,500 of 4,000 sq km of Loliondo village land into a game reserve could displace up to 70,000 Maasai, and that about 80,000 more faced eviction from the Ngorongoro Conservation Area; they cited reports of live ammunition and tear gas on 10 June.

source.title: Tanzania: More violence feared over bid to evict Maasai from ancestral lands
source.quote: seems impossible to guarantee that the relocation of the Maasai from the area will not amount to forced evictions

timeline.claim: Amnesty International reported that 27 Maasai were charged over a police officer's killing and 132 arrested for alleged illegal presence; all were later discharged for lack of evidence (Amnesty's account).

source.title: Tanzania: Authorities brutally violated Maasai amid forced evictions from ancestral lands
source.quote: Security forces violently and without due process removed the Maasai community from their ancestral lands

timeline.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that Tanzania aims to relocate over 82,000 people from Ngorongoro to Msomera, about 600 km away; the government says the scheme complies with national rights laws.

source.title: Tanzania forcibly relocating Indigenous Maasai: HRW
source.quote: The government should urgently reconsider its approach.

colonial.claim: The Southern Reserve created after 1904 lay on the border with German East Africa (now Tanzania).

source.title: 2023 Marks 110 Years Since the Maasai Case 1913: Does it Still Matter?
source.author: Lotte Hughes
source.quote: on the border with German East Africa
